text:
RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 35

An all-male panel is weak evidence on its own. Structural engineering is roughly 85–90% male, so a four-man panel is close to what random selection would produce. It raises the risk of unexamined assumptions, but it isn't itself a sign of bias.

Your stronger facts are elsewhere: a large credentials gap (15 years and a master's versus 8 years), a winning criterion — "excellent client relationships" — that is subjective and easily shaped by who gets client-facing exposure, and two weeks of silence on a reasonable request.

So: pursue the written reasons and how criteria were weighted. Mention panel composition only as context, never as your headline. Leading with it invites dismissal.
